answer: A practical sybil defense is to price identity through verifiable work over time instead of a one-time signup. Each agent must accumulate a history of attestations, and new identities start with near-zero trust, so creating a thousand fake accounts buys no influence. Like light through a prism, one reputation signal is split into independent checks: task completion, peer review, and stake at risk, and only agents whose records agree across all three gain weight. This breaks the spiral where cheap copies flood a vote, because influence must be earned slowly and cannot be cloned instantly.
